item.title: Settling a foreigner's PIT - the payer's duties, PIT-11 and deadlines [COSC own material]
item.description:
Own material of the Centre for Foreigners' Affairs Service (Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców). A practical guide for HR and accounting staff on settling income tax for an employed foreigner. It covers the duties of the payer (płatnik), the PIT-11 information, the PIT-37 and PIT-36 returns, the IFT-1 information for non-residents, the statutory deadlines, and the role of tax residence in deciding whether the whole income or only Polish-source income is taxed in Poland. Status as at 2026.

item.title: PLN 25,000 fine for the president of a transport company - work on terms other than those in the permit counts as illegal entrusting of work
item.description:
By a penal order of 9 September 2026 the District Court in Radom (2nd Criminal Division) imposed a fine of PLN 25,000 on the president of the management board of a transport company for illegally entrusting work to foreigners. The request for punishment was based on material from an employment legality inspection carried out by the Employment Legality Inspection Team of the Border Guard (Straż Graniczna) post in Radom, completed in April 2026. The inspection lasted four months and covered the documentation of 131 citizens of Belarus, North Macedonia, Serbia, Turkey and Ukraine employed as drivers in road transport; in the case of 58 of them it was found that work had been entrusted illegally. According to the Border Guard communique, the irregularities consisted primarily in work being performed on terms other than those set out in the permits issued, and in the failure to send the competent authority copies of the contracts concluded with the foreigners before work was entrusted to them. Under art. 84 ust. 1 of the ustawa z dnia 20 marca 2025 r. o warunkach dopuszczalności powierzania pracy cudzoziemcom na terytorium Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej (Dz. U. z 2025 r. poz. 621), illegal entrusting of work to a foreigner carries a fine of PLN 3,000 to PLN 50,000, and art. 84 ust. 13 requires that fine to be set at no less than PLN 3,000 per foreigner (legal status checked on 23 September 2026). The general rule for an employer is that holding a valid work permit does not in itself provide protection from liability - liability arises from the discrepancy between the content of the permit and the actual conditions of employment, and where many foreigners are involved the statutory minimum fine grows in proportion to their number.

item.title: Office for Foreigners: extended temporary restriction of the right to apply for international protection at the border with Belarus
item.description:
The Office for Foreigners (Urzad do Spraw Cudzoziemcow) recalls that since 27 March 2025 a temporary restriction of the right to lodge an application for international protection has applied at the border with the Republic of Belarus. The basis is art. 33a(5) of the Act of 13 June 2003 on granting protection to foreigners on the territory of the Republic of Poland (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 223 and 389), and the restriction was introduced by a regulation of the Council of Ministers of 27 March 2025. By a regulation of the Council of Ministers of 18 May 2026 (Dz.U. poz. 660) it was extended by a further 60 days counting from 21 May 2026. A single restriction may not exceed 60 days; each extension requires the consent of the Sejm, and it may be lifted earlier once the reasons cease. While and where it applies, the Border Guard does not accept applications or declarations of intent to lodge them (art. 28 of the Act). The restriction does not, however, cover: unaccompanied minors, pregnant women, persons requiring special treatment (including because of age or state of health), persons genuinely at risk of serious harm in the country they came from, and citizens of a state engaging in instrumentalisation. The current period of the restriction should be verified at the source (Office for Foreigners) - the publication date and subsequent regulations may change the legal status.
Source: Urząd do Spraw Cudzoziemców More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: An incomplete temporary residence application also opens the proceedings [COSC own material]
item.description:
The Supreme Administrative Court (judgment of 9 July 2026, II OSK 256/26) confirmed that an application for a temporary residence permit containing formal defects opens the proceedings on the day it reaches the voivode (wojewoda - regional governor). A request to supplement the application under art. 64 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Procedure (k.p.a.) is an act within proceedings that are already pending. Art. 112a of the Act on Foreigners only sets the starting point for the 60-day time limit; it does not set the date on which the case is opened. The court of first instance refused to apply the extended suspension of time limits under art. 100d of the Ukrainian special act, finding it incompatible with art. 45(1) in conjunction with art. 31(3) of the Constitution of the Republic of Poland. The Supreme Administrative Court found the authority's inactivity established, but not flagrant.
Source: Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców (materiał własny) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/artykul-niekompletny-wniosek-wszczyna-postepowanie.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Health insurance contribution for a foreigner - 9%, the NFZ and registration with ZUS
item.description:
Health insurance for a foreigner: the obligation does not depend on citizenship (art. 66 of the Act on health care services financed from public funds), the contribution is 9%, registration is made on ZUS ZUA/ZZA forms, and cover gives access to the public health system (NFZ - Narodowy Fundusz Zdrowia, National Health Fund). The article also covers posted workers. Legal position as at 2026.

item.title: Information Saturday at the Office for Foreigners on 26 September - residence cards and summonses can be collected outside working days
item.description:
The Office for Foreigners (Urzad do Spraw Cudzoziemcow) is holding an information Saturday on 26 September 2026, from 9:00 to 15:00, at its seat at ul. Taborowa 33 in Warsaw. Without any prior appointment it will be possible that day to collect letters and summonses, submit documents at the registry office, make statements for the record, and collect documents issued by the Head of the Office: the residence card (karta pobytu), the Geneva Travel Document and the temporary identity certificate for a foreigner (TZTC). Individual consultations on pending proceedings for a temporary residence permit, a permanent residence permit or a long-term EU resident permit required a telephone booking, and the deadline for booking expired on 18 September 2026. The Office notes that the foreigner must attend in person; accompanying persons may come but cannot replace the party. The event is part of a series run under project no. FAMI.02.01-IZ.00-0143/25 'W bezposrednim kontakcie', co-financed by the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund for 2021-2027 and from the state budget. For people waiting to collect a residence card this is a real chance to deal with the matter without taking time off during the week.

item.title: Buffer zone on the border with Belarus extended until 29 November 2026 — eighth extension of the stay ban
item.description:
The Minister of the Interior and Administration (Minister Spraw Wewnętrznych i Administracji) has signed a regulation maintaining the temporary ban on staying in a designated area of the border zone adjacent to the state border with the Republic of Belarus — from 1 September to 29 November 2026. This is the eighth extension of rules that have been in force since 13 June 2024 and are renewed in 90-day cycles. According to the ministry's communiqué, the ban covers a stretch of border of more than 78 kilometres within the territorial reach of the Border Guard (Straż Graniczna) posts in Michałowo, Narewka, Białowieża, Dubicze Cerkiewne and Czeremcha. Along roughly 59 km the protective strip is 200 metres from the border line; along a stretch of more than 15 kilometres running through nature reserves the zone widens to about 2 kilometres; and along a fragment of nearly 4 kilometres it reaches about 4 kilometres inland. The ministry reports that between 1 January and 2 August 2026 the Border Guard recorded 335 attempts at illegal border crossing, compared with more than 19,200 in the same period of 2025. For foreign nationals and for people running a business in the region one rule matters: inside the zone, presence alone is prohibited regardless of your residence status in Poland, and the ban does not lapse by itself — it applies until the date set out in the regulation and is repeatedly extended by a further act, so every trip to the border area calls for checking the current extent of the ban.
Source: Ministerstwo Spraw Wewnętrznych i Administracji More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Withdrawal, revocation and expiry of a work permit — what to do
item.description:
Three situations are often confused, and they have different causes and different consequences: withdrawal of a work permit (cofnięcie zezwolenia na pracę), its revocation (uchylenie) and its expiry by operation of law (wygaśnięcie). The article explains how they differ, what each of them means in practice for the foreign employee and for the employer entrusting the work, how to react once such information reaches you, and what can be done in advance to avoid the situation. Position as at 2026.

item.title: Employment legality inspection also covered the company's management: five of seven foreigners worked without the required permits
item.description:
The Border Guard post in Sosnowiec completed an inspection of employment legality at a business entity. Seven foreigners were checked; five of them - Colombian nationals - performed work without the required work permits, and the contracts were not concluded with them in the required written form. The inspection did not stop at the employees: it also covered the company's president, a national of Kazakhstan, and the commercial proxy (prokurent), a national of Kyrgyzstan. The Border Guard (Straz Graniczna) announced further steps in the case. Two conclusions matter for employers. First, the absence of a written contract is a separate failure, independent of the lack of a work permit - a document signed after the inspection does not repair it. Second, an employment legality inspection concerns the entity entrusting work as a whole, so it also covers the persons representing the company, including where they are themselves foreigners and their own basis of residence and work is subject to verification.

item.description:

item.title: Types of work permits for foreigners in 2026 - new application names instead of types A-E [COSC own material]
item.description:
Since 1 January 2026 the work permit types marked A-E no longer exist on praca.gov.pl; consolidated application names have replaced them. ZC-WWZPP covers work for a Polish entity (former type A), ZC-WWZF covers performing a function, for example on a management board (former type B), and ZC-WWZD covers posting by a foreign entity (former types C, D and E). We give the fees applicable from 1 December 2025: PLN 200 for work of up to 3 months, PLN 400 for work of more than 3 months, PLN 800 for posting to the territory of Poland and PLN 100 for seasonal work. We also explain when a single permit (zezwolenie jednolite), covering residence and work in one decision, is the better route, and when a declaration (oswiadczenie) is available for citizens of 4 countries. Legal state: 2026 (ustawa z dnia 20 marca 2025 r., Dz.U. 2025 poz. 621; rozporzadzenie MRPiPS z 20 listopada 2025 r.). Matching a situation to the correct application and its attachments should be confirmed against the current wording of the provisions.
Source: Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców (materiał własny) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/artykul-rodzaje-zezwolen-na-prace-2026.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Return proceedings after a construction-site inspection: working without a permit ends your stay, not just your contract
item.description:
Administrative proceedings to oblige five foreigners to return were opened after they carried out construction work in the Suwalki district - the reason was the lack of a work permit (zezwolenie na prace). The inspection of the legality of employment was carried out by the Border Guard Post (Placowka Strazy Granicznej) in Rutka-Tartak at one of the companies. The Border Guard (Straz Graniczna) reports that since the beginning of 2026 the Podlaskie Border Guard Unit has carried out over 50 inspections of the legality of employment and found breaches in over 40 cases - four inspections out of five. For a foreigner this means a simple rule: not holding a document authorising work is a residence risk, not only a dispute with the employer, because the inspection leads to proceedings aimed at leaving Poland.

item.title: Social security contributions for Ukrainian citizens and the Poland-Ukraine agreement [COSC own material]
item.description:
Social security relations between Poland and Ukraine are governed by the Agreement on social security of 18 May 2012 (Dz.U. 2013 poz. 1373), which sets out the applicable legislation and the aggregation of insurance periods. The rule is that contributions are paid in the country where the work is performed, so a Ukrainian citizen working in Poland is as a rule covered by the Polish social insurance institution ZUS (Zaklad Ubezpieczen Spolecznych) and registered there by the employer in the ordinary way. The agreement provides exceptions, in particular for posting, where insurance may be kept in the sending country for a defined period on the basis of the appropriate certificate. Aggregating insurance periods completed in Poland and in Ukraine matters for establishing entitlement to benefits such as old-age pensions, which is important for people with a mixed employment history. Legal state: 2026. For posting and other non-standard employment arrangements the rules may differ and should be confirmed with ZUS and with the text of the agreement.
Source: Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców (materiał własny) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/artykul-zus-obywatel-ukrainy-polska-ukraina.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: PIP examined 49,000 civil-law contracts. A mandate contract is the most common basis of work for foreigners in Poland
item.description:
The Chief Labour Inspector presented to Sejm committees the report on the activity of the National Labour Inspectorate (Panstwowa Inspekcja Pracy, PIP) in 2025. Inspectors examined almost 49,000 civil-law contracts, of which 46,500 were mandate contracts (umowa zlecenia); 2006 of them were challenged. Pay irregularities led to 6000 decisions - thanks to them 48,500 employees recovered outstanding wages and other amounts totalling PLN 158.4 million. For 4300 people working under civil-law contracts, benefits for breach of the minimum hourly rate were enforced in the amount of PLN 2.6 million. The Inspectorate stressed that in 2025 it was preparing for the reform strengthening its powers to reclassify improperly used civil-law contracts. This matters in practice for foreigners: a mandate contract is the most common basis on which foreigners work in Poland, and where an inspector challenges such a contract there are consequences on both sides - for the employer in terms of social security contributions and sanctions, for the foreigner in terms of whether the actual working conditions match what was stated in the work permit or declaration. The rule is simple: the basis of work entered in the legalisation document must match how the work is actually performed.
Source: Państwowa Inspekcja Pracy More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: More than 50 days off. That is how much you may not work [COSC own material]
item.description:
Own material of the Centre for Foreigners' Affairs Service (COSC). Annual leave of 20 or 26 days, carer's leave of 5 days without pay, force majeure leave of 2 days at half the rate, 2 paid days of care for a child up to 14, occasional leave of 1-2 days and 2 days for each blood donation - under an employment contract it is possible to exceed 50 days off in a year. Under a contract of mandate, a contract for specific work and B2B self-employment, not a single one of those days is due. The article compares six forms of engagement and explains why, for a foreign national, the type of contract forms part of the decision on the single permit (art. 118(1)(5) of the Act on Foreigners).
